query: adaptive user simulator reward design LLM agents
text:
1. **[EAU: Environment-Agent-User Co-evolution for Training User-Centric Agents](https://arxiv.org/html/2610.16523v1)** — October 2026. Closest match: a meta-agent adapts user simulators, environments, reward design, and RL settings during training. **People:** Min Cai (University of Alberta); Dan Zhang (National University of Singapore); Gao Xing and Libin Ma (Kuaishou Technology); Zhaohui Xu (independent researcher); Xi Ye (University of Alberta and Amii).

2. **[Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning for Tool-Calling Agents with Iterative Reward Calibration](https://arxiv.org/html/2604.02869v1)** — April 2026. Studies how poorly designed per-turn rewards undermine learning with simulated users, and introduces calibration based on training trajectories. **People:** Wachiravit Modecrua, Krittanon Kaewtawee, Krittin Pachtrachai, and Touchapon Kraisingkorn — Amity Research and Application Center (ARAC).

3. **[Learning User Simulators with Turing Rewards](https://arxiv.org/html/2606.19336v1)** — June 2026. Trains simulators using rewards for responses indistinguishable from real users’ responses. **People:** Yingshan Susan Wang, Cedegao E. Zhang, Linlu Qiu, Zexue He, Pengyuan Li, Alex Pentland, Roger P. Levy, and Yoon Kim. **Affiliations listed:** MIT, Stanford University, and MIT-IBM Watson AI Lab.

4. **[World Model-Guided Reinforcement Learning via Counterfactual User Engagement Simulation](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.01067v1)** — September 2026. Uses simulated user feedback on alternative recommendations to generate dense rewards for agent training. **People:** Ang Li, Bin Liang, and Kam-Fai Wong (Chinese University of Hong Kong); Xin Xu, Yue Ma, and Fubang Zhao (ByteDance); Yangyang Kang (Zhejiang University and ByteDance).

query: within-run and across-run adaptation agent training
text:
The closest matches use the terms **in-context adaptation**, **cross-episode learning**, and **meta-reinforcement learning**. Affiliations below are those listed in the papers.

1. **[Meta-RL Induces Exploration in Language Agents — LaMer](https://arxiv.org/html/2512.16848v2)** (2025; revised 2026). Trains agents across successive attempts, using feedback and reflection to adapt without test-time gradient updates. **People:** Yulun Jiang (EPFL, ETH Zurich); Liangze Jiang (EPFL, Idiap Research Institute); Damien Teney (Idiap); Michael Moor (ETH Zurich); Maria Brbić (EPFL).

2. **[Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2303.11366)** (2023). Particularly relevant to across-run adaptation: agents retain reflections from previous trials to improve subsequent attempts, without updating model weights. **People:** Noah Shinn, Federico Cassano, Edward Berman (Northeastern University); Ashwin Gopinath (MIT); Karthik Narasimhan, Shunyu Yao (Princeton University).

3. **[RL²: Fast Reinforcement Learning via Slow Reinforcement Learning](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1611.02779)** (2016). Foundational work connecting fast adaptation during interaction with slower training across tasks; recurrent memory persists across episodes. **People:** Yan Duan, John Schulman, Xi Chen, Pieter Abbeel (UC Berkeley and OpenAI); Peter L. Bartlett (UC Berkeley); Ilya Sutskever (OpenAI).

4. **[Learning to Adapt in Dynamic, Real-World Environments Through Meta-Reinforcement Learning](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1803.11347)** (ICLR 2019). Strong match for within-run adaptation: agents continually adapt a learned dynamics model using recent experience, handling unexpected changes during operation. **People:** Anusha Nagabandi, Ignasi Clavera, Simin Liu, Ronald S. Fearing, Pieter Abbeel, Sergey Levine, Chelsea Finn (UC Berkeley).

1. **[SEAL: Synergistic Co-Evolution of Agents and Learning Environments](https://arxiv.org/html/2605.24426v1)** — May 2026. Uses diagnosed agent failures to jointly improve tool-use policies and learning environments. **People:** Yihao Hu, Zhihao Wen, Xiujin Liu, Pan Wang, Xin Zhang, Wei Wu. **Team affiliations:** Ant Group, Westlake University, University of Michigan–Ann Arbor, University of Science and Technology of China.

2. **[GenEnv: Difficulty-Aligned Co-Evolution Between LLM Agents and Environment Simulators](https://arxiv.org/html/2512.19682v2)** — December 2025. Co-trains an agent and an environment simulator that generates tasks matched to the agent’s evolving abilities. **Lead authors:** Jiacheng Guo and Ling Yang (**Princeton**), Peter Chen (**Columbia**), Qixin Xiao (**University of Michigan**), with collaborators.

3. **[Co-Evolution in Agentic Systems: Toward Self-Directed Evolution Beyond Human Design](https://arxiv.org/html/2608.10299v1)** — August 2026. A survey covering agent–agent, agent–environment, and meta co-evolution; useful for finding related work. **People:** Qing Zong, Jiayu Liu, Junhao Shen, Zecong Tang, et al. **Team affiliations:** HKUST, University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, Chinese University of Hong Kong, University of Hong Kong, Peking University.

4. **[Environment Evolution for Terminal Agents](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.04128v1)** — September 2026. Closely related work that progressively increases environment difficulty and compares this approach with agent–environment co-evolution. **People:** Zhiyuan Fan, Tinghao Yu, Yuanjun Cai, Jiang Zhou, et al. **Affiliation:** Tencent’s Hunyuan Team.

query: LLM agent training environment evolves with policy
text:
1. **[EAU: Environment-Agent-User Co-evolution for Training User-Centric Agents](https://arxiv.org/html/2610.16523v1)** — October 2026. Closest match: a meta-agent modifies the environment, simulated user, rewards, and training configuration while the policy learns.
   **People:** Min Cai (University of Alberta); Dan Zhang (National University of Singapore); Gao Xing and Libin Ma (Kuaishou Technology); Zhaohui Xu (independent researcher); Xi Ye (University of Alberta and Amii).

2. **[SEAL: Synergistic Co-Evolution of Agents and Learning Environments](https://arxiv.org/html/2605.24426v1)** — May 2026. Uses failed agent trajectories to jointly improve the environment’s tool cues and feedback and update the policy.
   **People:** Yihao Hu, Zhihao Wen, Xiujin Liu, Pan Wang, Xin Zhang, and Wei Wu. **Affiliations listed:** Ant Group, Westlake University, University of Michigan–Ann Arbor, and University of Science and Technology of China; the HTML does not clearly map individual authors to institutions.

3. **[CoEvolve: Training LLM Agents via Agent-Data Mutual Evolution](https://arxiv.org/html/2604.15840v1)** — April 2026. A related approach: training tasks evolve with the agent, using rollout feedback to synthesize and validate tasks targeting current weaknesses.
   **People:** Shidong Yang, Ziyu Ma, Tongwen Huang, Yiming Hu, Yong Wang, and Xiangxiang Chu — all affiliated with AMAP, Alibaba Group.

query: multi-turn reinforcement learning user simulation benchmarks
text:
1. **[LMRL Gym: Benchmarks for Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning with Language Models](https://lmrl-gym.github.io/)** — Closest match: eight interactive tasks with datasets and simulators for RL training and evaluation, including information gathering and negotiation. **People:** Marwa Abdulhai, Isadora White, Charlie Snell, Charles Sun, Joey Hong, and Yuexiang Zhai (UC Berkeley); Kelvin Xu (Google DeepMind); Sergey Levine (both).

2. **[UserRL: Training Interactive User-Centric Agent via Reinforcement Learning](https://lifelongagent.github.io/Project-Lifelong-Agent/UserRL/index.html)** — Eight gym environments pairing simulated users with multi-turn RL; studies how reward design and simulator choice affect learning. **People:** Cheng Qian and Heng Ji (University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign); Zuxin Liu, Akshara Prabhakar, Jielin Qiu, and colleagues (Salesforce AI Research).

3. **[UserBench: An Interactive Gym Environment for User-Centric Agents](https://arxiv.org/html/2507.22034v1)** — Benchmark and training environment where simulated users gradually reveal preferences, testing clarification, tool use, and user alignment. Supports multi-turn RL with customizable rewards. **People:** Cheng Qian (Salesforce AI Research and UIUC), Heng Ji (UIUC), and Zuxin Liu, Akshara Prabhakar, Zhiwei Liu, Jianguo Zhang, and colleagues (Salesforce AI Research).

4. **[SimulatorArena: Are User Simulators Reliable Proxies for Multi-Turn Evaluation of AI Assistants?](https://aclanthology.org/2025.emnlp-main.1786.pdf)** — Especially relevant for validating simulators: 909 annotated human–LLM conversations covering math tutoring and document creation. Evaluates simulation fidelity rather than RL algorithms. **People:** Yao Dou, Alan Ritter, and Wei Xu (Georgia Tech); Michel Galley, Baolin Peng, Chris Kedzie, Weixin Cai, Chris Quirk, and Jianfeng Gao (Microsoft; paper notes Kedzie subsequently joined Scaled Cognition).

query: editable training systems for tool-using agents
text:
1. **[EAU: Environment-Agent-User Co-evolution for Training User-Centric Agents](https://arxiv.org/html/2610.16523v1)** — The closest match: a meta-agent edits user simulators, environments, rewards, and RL settings, validating and applying changes during training. **People:** Min Cai (University of Alberta); Dan Zhang (National University of Singapore); Gao Xing and Libin Ma (Kuaishou Technology); Zhaohui Xu (independent researcher); Xi Ye (University of Alberta and Amii).

2. **[Agent Lightning: Train ANY AI Agents with Reinforcement Learning](https://arxiv.org/html/2508.03680v1)** — A modular training framework that separates agent execution from RL, supporting customizable rewards and existing tool-using workflows. **People:** Xufang Luo, Yuge Zhang, Zhiyuan He, Zilong Wang, Siyun Zhao, Dongsheng Li, Luna K. Qiu, and Yuqing Yang — Microsoft Research.

3. **[Agent Learning via Early Experience](https://openreview.net/pdf/b090aea758a96038a0c9b91036f8cf16813fb4bc.pdf)** — Related work on training agents from exploratory interactions and self-reflection without reward signals; less directly about editable training infrastructure. **People include:** Kai Zhang (Meta Superintelligence Labs and Ohio State); Xiangchao Chen, Huan Sun, and Yu Su (Ohio State); Bo Liu and Jason Weston (FAIR at Meta); Yifan Wu (Meta Superintelligence Labs).

query: methods improving user-centric agents with simulated users
text:
1. **[Training Proactive and Personalized LLM Agents (2025)](https://arxiv.org/html/2511.02208v1)** — The closest match: introduces **UserVille**, simulated users with configurable preferences, and **PPP**, reinforcement learning that jointly rewards task success, useful clarification, and personalization.  
   **People and affiliations:** Weiwei Sun, Xuhui Zhou, Weihua Du, Sean Welleck, Graham Neubig, Maarten Sap, and Yiming Yang; Xingyao Wang. The team spans **Carnegie Mellon University and OpenHands**.

2. **[UserBench: An Interactive Gym Environment for User-Centric Agents (2025)](https://arxiv.org/html/2507.22034v1)** — An evaluation and training environment where simulated users reveal preferences gradually and indirectly, testing whether agents ask effective questions and satisfy underlying intent.  
   **People and affiliations:** Cheng Qian (**Salesforce AI Research; University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign**), Heng Ji (**UIUC**), and Zuxin Liu, Akshara Prabhakar, Zhiwei Liu, Jianguo Zhang, Haolin Chen, Weiran Yao, Shelby Heinecke, Silvio Savarese, Caiming Xiong, and Huan Wang (**Salesforce AI Research**).

3. **[Learning User Simulators with Turing Rewards (2026)](https://arxiv.org/html/2606.19336v1)** — Improves the simulated users themselves: **Turing-RL** rewards responses that judges cannot distinguish from real users’ responses, conditioned on user history. Relevant infrastructure for agent training and personalization evaluation.  
   **People and affiliations:** Yingshan Susan Wang, Cedegao E. Zhang, Linlu Qiu, Zexue He, Pengyuan Li, Alex Pentland, Roger P. Levy, and Yoon Kim; affiliations include **MIT, Stanford University, and the MIT-IBM Watson AI Lab**.
